title: revl composition interchange (manifest + G8 audit)
description: The versioned, tool-consumable verdict a revl gate produces for a composition: what each component provides, requires, and reaches (its G8 boundary surface), plus the declared host-code externs and the per-service distributability verdict. A consumer can read provides/requires/reaches from this document WITHOUT running revl. See docs/interchange-format.md for the compatibility promise.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR of this interchange format. Same MAJOR is backward compatible: a consumer written for X.m keeps reading X.n (n>m); new MINOR versions only add optional members. A MAJOR bump may remove or re-shape members.

kind.description: Self-identifying tag so a consumer can tell an interchange document apart from any other JSON. Always the constant below for this format.

boundary.description: Per-component G8 boundary surface, keyed by component name. This is the 'reaches' half of provides/requires/reaches.

externs.description: Every declared host-code extern in the composition (the trust surface a proof cannot cover).

distributability.description: Per-service verdict on whether the service may cross a process seam (interop-bridge §4), keyed by service name.

cardinality.description: Optional (item 260). Per-component per-capability crossing-count ceiling per activation, keyed by component name. Present only for components that cross an emission boundary, so a crossing-free composition carries an empty object. A capability whose multiplicity is not statically provable (a loop, any recursion, a first-class emitting arrow, a crossing behind a host extern) is `unbounded` with `bound: null` and a `reason`; the component `verdict` rolls the tokens up with `unbounded` dominating.

gauntlet.description: Optional. A gauntlet dossier (docs/gauntlet.md) carried in the same envelope. Its proved/tested/claimed/pending sections reuse the manifest+boundary vocabulary defined here, so item 31's dossier composes into this format without a schema change. Left open (additionalProperties) so the dossier can evolve independently.

manifest.description: The linker's composition manifest: the static membership, load order, and each component's provide/require/isolate/intercept surface.

loadOrder.description: Component names in dependency order (providers first). Teardown is the exact reverse (LIFO).

templates.description: Optional. Instance-parametric components: spawn targets instantiated at runtime, each in its own local realm, excluded from the static composition.

isolate.description: Optional. provision-key -> realm name, when a key is bound in a named local realm.

intercept.description: Optional. provision-key -> interception metadata for keys this component intercepts.

emissions.description: Emission call sites (irreversible boundary crossings) this component performs, as `key.method` labels.

capabilities.description: emission-label -> the capability scopes its declaration carries. A single-element list of "*" is a bare emission that promises nothing about where it goes.

compensated.description: How many of this component's emissions carry a compensating undo.

awaits.description: Iteration/await boundaries in this component's body.

externs.description: Host-code externs this component reaches, transitively through functions. A first-class dispatch appears as name "*" with class "first-class dispatch".

class.description: The extern's classification, one of the four G4 boundary classes: "pure" (no observable effect), "acquire" (takes a resource that must be released), "emission" (an irreversible crossing out of the system), or "witnessed" (a reversible host mutation that names its inverse). The pseudo-class "first-class dispatch" appears (with name "*") for a reach through a value whose target is not statically nameable. May be null when unknown.

capabilities.description: The declared capability scope of a scoped `emission[...]`/`witnessed[...]` extern, as a sorted list of tokens (e.g. ["fs"]). This token — not the extern name — is what a `capability <glob>` policy rule and the register floor key on. Absent for an unscoped extern, whose token is its own name. This is the machine-readable form of the ` [fs]` clause on the human render's `host code:` line.

backends.description: Backend tiers this extern has a body for (sorted), e.g. ["py"]. This is the machine-readable form of the tier the human render prints after the class, as in `(witnessed, py)`.

per_capability.description: Capability token -> its per-activation crossing ceiling.

bound.description: The proved per-activation maximum, or null when unbounded.

reason.description: Present when kind is unbounded: why the multiplicity is not statically provable.
